## Preface

Try not to become a man of success, but rather try to become a man of value.

—Albert Einstein

My late father was a successful serial entrepreneur. Over the course of a prolific 70‐year career, he operated and invested in restaurants, pharmacies, amusement parks, and eventually moved to property development and hospitality operations. His investments yielded not just profit but valuable insight into the mechanisms of how businesses work. Most were successful, but some weren't, and by the time I was ready to embark on a career, he was prepared to send me into the world with advice culled from years of experience. His most valuable guidance dealt not with what I should do, but what I should not do: namely, to steer clear of professions weighted with labor, rent, and inventory.

"Any labor‐intensive business will likely lead to human politics, so look for those that require minimal manpower," my father said. "Besides, international cities like Hong Kong are infamous for high rents, which will squeeze into margins and profits, so avoid a business that requires a prestigious location. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
